text.tspan: The repetition penalty — a brake on repeating
the rule and its signs · the effect on probabilities · the untrained loop, step by step · how strong a brake
The loop and the sweep are the untrained model’s real greedy decoding; the row of five
A model that has just written a word often gives that same word a high score again, and greedy decoding can then loop forever — “resort resort resort …”. The repetition penalty (Keskar et al.,
, CTRL) lowers the score of every token already in the answer, before the next one is chosen.

text.tspan: The penalty applies once per step, whatever the count: a word written five times is pushed down no harder than one written once. A mild penalty only delays the loop; a strong one breaks it sooner — and would also push down words that SHOULD repeat, like “the” in “the cat sat on the sofa”. On a trained model, which is already sure
of each word, the penalty at
the untrained model leaves one loop for another
it runs before the choice, so greedy decoding changes too
correct repeats (“the … the”) get pushed down too
